Remote cybersecurity internship, open worldwide

SkillMe's cybersecurity internship is remote and open worldwide: 4 weeks, one reviewed milestone a week, about 2–3 hours each. You build a Python security tool: a password breach checker, a brute-force login detector or a file integrity monitor. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

The Cybersecurity internship in short

In the SkillMe Cybersecurity internship you build one of 3 projects, such as PassGuard: Password Strength & Breach Checker, a project where you build a Python tool that rates password strength and safely checks whether a password has appeared in known data breaches. In week 1 you write a command-line Python program that scores a password and explains how to make it stronger. By week 4 you add a secure passphrase generator and wrap everything in a simple web interface. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

What you build

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

You are assigned one of these projects when you start, and build it milestone by milestone.

PassGuard: Password Strength & Breach Checker

Build a Python tool that rates password strength and safely checks whether a password has appeared in known data breaches.

  1. W1Password Strength Rules in Python
  2. W2Entropy and Common Password Detection
  3. W3Safe Breach Check with k-Anonymity
  4. W4Passphrase Generator and Web UI

LogSentry: Brute-force Login Detector

Build a Python tool that reads login logs and flags suspicious repeated failed sign-ins.

  1. W1Reading and Parsing Log Files
  2. W2Detecting Repeated Failed Logins
  3. W3Real Log Formats and Alert Reports
  4. W4Dashboard and Incident Summary

FileWatch: File Integrity Monitor

Build a Python tool that detects when files in a folder are added, changed or deleted using cryptographic hashes.

  1. W1Hashing Files in Python
  2. W2Baseline and Change Detection
  3. W3Continuous Monitoring and Alerts
  4. W4Integrity Report and Dashboard
Week by week

What each week of the Cybersecurity internship covers

Shown for PassGuard: Password Strength & Breach Checker. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Password Strength Rules in Python

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Write a command-line Python program that scores a password and explains how to make it stronger. This teaches the basics of what makes passwords weak and gets your project set up for the coming weeks.

    What you learn

    • Ethics and law: only test systems you own or have written permission to test
    • What makes a password weak: length, variety and predictability
    • Python strings, conditions and functions
    • Reading input safely with getpass so passwords are not shown on screen

    What you submit

    • passguard.py command-line tool
    • README with the legal and ethical note and usage instructions
    • Screenshot or short video of the tool rating 3 sample passwords
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • The tool rates abc123 as Weak and a long mixed password as Strong
    • Each missing rule produces a clear tip
    • The password is not shown on screen while typing
    • The README contains the legal and ethical note

    Stretch goal: Load a small list of the most common passwords from a text file and mark any match as Weak immediately.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Entropy and Common Password Detection

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Make your checker smarter by estimating password entropy and detecting common patterns like dictionary words and keyboard sequences. You will also add automated tests so you can change code with confidence.

    What you learn

    • Password entropy as a simple measure of guessing difficulty
    • Detecting common patterns such as qwerty, 1234 and repeated characters
    • Writing unit tests with pytest

    What you submit

    • Updated passguard.py with entropy and pattern checks
    • common.txt word list
    • test_passguard.py with at least 8 passing tests
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • The tool shows an estimated entropy in bits
    • Password2024! is flagged for a common word and year pattern
    • pytest runs at least 8 tests and all pass
    • Scores stay the same for the Week 1 examples unless a new check applies

    Stretch goal: Estimate the time to guess the password at a given number of guesses per second and show it in plain English.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Safe Breach Check with k-Anonymity

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Check whether a password has appeared in known breaches using the Have I Been Pwned range API, without ever sending the password itself. You will learn how hashing and k-anonymity protect privacy, and how to handle network errors.

    What you learn

    • Hashing with SHA-1 using Python's hashlib
    • How k-anonymity lets you query a service without revealing the password
    • Making HTTP requests with requests
    • Handling timeouts and network errors gracefully

    What you submit

    • Breach check feature in passguard.py
    • README section explaining k-anonymity with a simple diagram
    • Tests for the breach check using a mocked response
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • password is reported as breached with a count greater than zero
    • Only the 5-character hash prefix is sent over the network
    • The tool shows a friendly error and does not crash when offline
    • All tests pass without an internet connection

    Stretch goal: Add a local cache of prefix responses so repeated checks do not call the API again.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    Passphrase Generator and Web UI

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Add a secure passphrase generator and wrap everything in a simple web interface. Finish with a clear README and a demo that explains how the tool protects user privacy.

    What you learn

    • Generating secure random values with Python's secrets module
    • Building a simple UI with Streamlit or Flask
    • Writing clear security documentation

    What you submit

    • Passphrase generator feature
    • Web UI for PassGuard
    • Final README with privacy explanation
    • Demo video
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • Generated passphrases use the secrets module, not random
    • The web UI shows strength, entropy and breach results
    • No password is written to logs or files
    • All earlier tests still pass
    • Someone can run the app from the README instructions

    Stretch goal: Add a 'copy to clipboard' button and a strength meter bar that updates as the user types.

Is it for you?

This internship fits you if

  • You know the basics of Web Security, Python and OWASP and want a real project to show for it, not more tutorials.

  • You can give it about 2-3 hours a week around college or a job, from any country.

Cybersecurity internship: questions and answers

Is the cybersecurity internship remote and open worldwide?

Yes. It is a fully remote cybersecurity internship and you can apply from any country.

Is this a cybersecurity internship with stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. 8–10 interns are picked each month from those who complete the internship and hold an issued certificate. It is not paid to every intern.

What will I build in the Cybersecurity internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: PassGuard: Password Strength & Breach Checker, LogSentry: Brute-force Login Detector or FileWatch: File Integrity Monitor. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the Cybersecurity internship?

The Cybersecurity internship works with Web Security, Python and OWASP. Week 1: ethics and law: only test systems you own or have written permission to test; what makes a password weak: length, variety and predictability. Week 2: password entropy as a simple measure of guessing difficulty; detecting common patterns such as qwerty, 1234 and repeated characters. Week 3: hashing with SHA-1 using Python's hashlib; how k-anonymity lets you query a service without revealing the password. Week 4: generating secure random values with Python's secrets module; building a simple UI with Streamlit or Flask.

Do I need experience to apply for the Cybersecurity internship?

You need the basics of Web Security, Python and OWASP, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you write a command-line Python program that scores a password and explains how to make it stronger. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each Cybersecurity milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of PassGuard: Password Strength & Breach Checker, that means: the tool rates abc123 as Weak and a long mixed password as Strong; each missing rule produces a clear tip; the password is not shown on screen while typing; the README contains the legal and ethical note. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the Cybersecurity internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Built a Python password strength checker with clear improvement tips; Used getpass so passwords are never displayed or stored; Learned the basics of password security and ethical testing; Added entropy estimation and common-pattern detection to my password checker; Wrote 8+ unit tests with pytest; Learned why long passwords can still be weak; Added a privacy-preserving breach check using SHA-1 and k-anonymity; Integrated the Have I Been Pwned range API with error handling; Wrote tests with mocked network calls; Built a secure passphrase generator with Python's secrets module; Shipped a web interface for my password strength and breach checker; Documented how the tool protects user privacy.

What are the other projects in the Cybersecurity internship?

LogSentry: Brute-force Login Detector: Build a Python tool that reads login logs and flags suspicious repeated failed sign-ins. FileWatch: File Integrity Monitor: Build a Python tool that detects when files in a folder are added, changed or deleted using cryptographic hashes. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the Cybersecurity internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based: 8–10 interns are picked each month from those who complete the internship and hold an issued certificate. It is not paid to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
